en: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Farabi
tr: Ebû Nasr Muhammed b. Muhammed el-Fârâbî
ar: أبو نصر محمد بن محمد الفارابي

description.tr: 'İkinci Muallim' (Aristoteles'ten sonra) — Platon ve Aristoteles'i İbn Sînâ ve İbn Rüşd'ün üzerine inşa ettiği İslami felsefi çerçevede sentezledi. Ayrıca ortaçağın en önemli müzik teorisi risalesini yazdı || Fârâbî, 500 yıl boyunca İslam felsefesini belirleyen felsefi terminoloji ve metodolojiyi yarattı. || [Tarih notu] Walzer'in 1985 kritik edisyonu Fârâbî'nin özgünlüğünü yeniden kurdu.
description.en: The 'Second Teacher' (after Aristotle) — synthesized Plato and Aristotle into an Islamic philosophical framework that Ibn Sina and Ibn Rushd built upon. Also wrote the most important medieval treatise on music theory || Farabi created the philosophical vocabulary and methodology that defined Islamic philosophy for 500 years. His emanationist cosmology harmonized Aristotelian logic with Islamic monotheism. Ibn Sina called him the greatest philosopher after Aristotle — hence 'Second Teacher.' || [Historiographical note] Walzer's 1985 critical edition of al-Madina al-Fadila reestablished Farabi's originality. Mahdi (2001) demonstrated his political philosophy was more than Platonic imitation.
description.ar: المعلم الثاني (بعد أرسطو) — جمع بين أفلاطون وأرسطو في إطار فلسفي إسلامي بنى عليه ابن سينا وابن رشد. وكتب أهم رسالة في نظرية الموسيقى || أنشأ الفارابي المصطلحات والمنهجية الفلسفية التي حددت الفلسفة الإسلامية لخمسة قرون. وفّق بين المنطق الأرسطي والتوحيد الإسلامي من خلال نظرية الفيض
